doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Teacher first: fitting 80 concerts a year around teaching
summary: DiMartino says teaching came first; he taught all week and flew out for concerts, pre-teaching students if away over four days.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well first of all, I’m a teacher first. I’ve always wanted to be just like my high school band director, so I always made sure that I taught all my students every week and never missed any, because that was my primary goal, is to be an asset to that community no matter where I was teaching. It didn’t really matter if I was teaching junior high school students I would be the same. And then on the weekends, you know I would teach until Thursday afternoon and then I could get on a plane and I could fly to another university or some concert venue, you know, to play with some other folks: a brass quintet, jazz groups, a solo with wind ensembles, and stuff like that. And then I would come back on Sunday night.

There’s a lot to be said for that because I’m familiar with a number of people who are educators but they don’t have the same philosophy about that. They will reschedule lessons at the drop of a hat because they have a gig.

Right. Well you know to some degree I very rarely did anything longer than three or four days. It looks like I was gone forever you know, but I did an average of — I remember when I filled out my university forms you know every year they want to know what you’ve done. I usually had about — between my regional concerts and my other concerts, I had about 80 a year. So it looks like oh my God how did anybody do that. Well if it’s just like a local brass quintet gig it just says “and others” you know, but these were things that were actually formal concerts of some sort. local, meaning in a hundred mile radius. And then some of them were — you know. And if I did have to leave more than four days I pre-taught my students before I left. I never wanted to be trying to play catch-up you know. That put me at ease both performing and teaching.
